title: Babylon Invades Judah

questions.question: Who became the servant of Nebuchadnezzar for three years?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 24:1 (ESV): "...Jehoiakim became his servant three years; then he turned and rebelled against him."

questions.question: Who succeeded Jehoiakim?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 24:6 (ESV): "So Jehoiakim slept with his fathers, and Jehoiachin his son reigned in his place."

questions.question: What did Nebuchadnezzar carry away from Jerusalem?
options: All the treasures of the house of the LORD and the king's house, and the people
questions.correctAnswer: All the treasures of the house of the LORD and the king's house, and the people
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 24:13-14 (ESV): "and carried off all the treasures... He carried away all Jerusalem..."

questions.question: Who did the King of Babylon make king in place of Jehoiachin?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 24:17 (ESV): "And the king of Babylon made Mattaniah, Jehoiachin's uncle, king in his place, and changed his name to Zedekiah."

questions.question: What did Zedekiah do regarding the King of Babylon?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 24:20 (ESV): "...And Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon."

questions.question: How long did Jehoiachin reign?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 24:8 (ESV): "...and he reigned three months in Jerusalem."

questions.question: Who did the Lord send against Jehoiakim to destroy Judah?
options: Bands of the Chaldeans, Syrians, Moabites, and Ammonites
questions.correctAnswer: Bands of the Chaldeans, Syrians, Moabites, and Ammonites
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 24:2 (ESV): "And the LORD sent against him bands of the Chaldeans and bands of the Syrians..."

questions.question: Why did this happen to Judah?
options: Surely this came upon Judah at the command of the LORD, to remove them out of his sight, for the sins of Manasseh
questions.correctAnswer: Surely this came upon Judah at the command of the LORD, to remove them out of his sight, for the sins of Manasseh
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 24:3 (ESV): "Surely this came upon Judah at the command of the LORD... for the sins of Manasseh..."

questions.question: Who surrendered to the King of Babylon?
options: Jehoiachin, his mother, his servants, his officials, and palace officials
questions.correctAnswer: Jehoiachin, his mother, his servants, his officials, and palace officials
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 24:12 (ESV): "and Jehoiachin the king of Judah gave himself up to the king of Babylon, himself and his mother..."

questions.question: How many people did the king of Babylon carry captive in total (soldiers and craftsmen)?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 24:14 (ESV): "He carried away all Jerusalem... ten thousand captives..."

questions.question: Who was left in the land?
options: Only the poorest people of the land
questions.correctAnswer: Only the poorest people of the land
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 24:14 (ESV): "...None remained, except the poorest people of the land."

questions.question: How many men of valor were carried away?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 24:16 (ESV): "And the king of Babylon brought captive to Babylon the seven thousand men of valor..."

questions.question: How many craftsmen and metal workers were carried away?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 24:16 (ESV): "...and the craftsmen and the metal workers, one thousand..."

questions.question: Who was Jehoiachin's mother?
options: Nehushta the daughter of Elnathan of Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: Nehushta the daughter of Elnathan of Jerusalem
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 24:8 (ESV): "...His mother's name was Nehushta the daughter of Elnathan of Jerusalem."

questions.question: Did the King of Egypt come out of his land again?
options: No, for the king of Babylon had taken all that belonged to him
questions.correctAnswer: No, for the king of Babylon had taken all that belonged to him
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 24:7 (ESV): "And the king of Egypt did not come again out of his land..."

key_verse_text: Surely this came upon Judah at the command of the LORD, to remove them out of his sight, for the sins of Manasseh, according to all that he had done. (ESV)
